question.question:
Use exact arithmetic. A firm has unlevered asset value 1750 USD million, existing debt 225 USD million (carrying no tax-shield value) and 40 million shares. It plans to issue 450 USD million of new perpetual debt, pay an underwriting fee of 3 percent of the amount actually issued (a cash outflow that reduces firm value) and spend all net proceeds on a share repurchase. Each dollar of new debt issued adds 26 percent of face value in permanent tax-shield value. A covenant caps total debt (existing plus new) divided by post-repurchase equity value at 0.8; if the planned issue would breach it, the issue is scaled down to the largest amount that exactly meets the limit. Post-repurchase equity value equals unlevered asset value plus tax shield minus fee minus total debt. Shares are repurchased at the self-consistent price: equity value just after the issue, with net proceeds still held as cash, divided by the original share count; retiring shares leaves the price unchanged. Report the number of shares outstanding after the repurchase, in millions.

Answer format: use exact arithmetic through all intermediate steps, round only the final value half up to 4 decimal digits, and return only the numeric value interpreted in `count` with no unit label or additional text.

slots.description: New debt actually issued after applying the covenant cap.
Self-consistent per-share price at which shares are repurchased.
Equity value remaining after the repurchase is completed.
